purpose: Persistent actor renderer history and ordered semantic erase/draw/overlay/reset decisions, shared by gameplay and demos. Pixel services and all surrounding frame work retain their existing owners.

inputs: ActorRenderStorage persists across mode switches for all16 physical slots; one physical slot index, operation, raw fixed position, simulation sprite and gameplay overlay. All scalar history words and position words are admitted, including stale values.
No ActorType, ActorPhase, semantic scratch alias or page-derived replacement cache is read. Active-prefix/sentinel iteration stays in the literal bridge shell.
outputs: Updated selected typed history; at most five ordered store/draw/restore events. Reset also emits the current simulation sprite hide.
effects: Requests include exact sprite identity and wrapping pixel coordinates; they contain no pointer, register or VGA representation. Store and service events are interleaved, including main restore before overlay cache swap.

Pixel services are synchronous L1 calls with original near return words and actual register/flag/device effects. An abnormal return commits exactly the consumed prefix; normal return rejects any leftover request.
preconditions: Ordinary disjoint data/resources/native outputs and stack; pixel services do not mutate actor arrays, preserve SI/DS/CS/SS:SP and retain their actual machine outputs. No asynchronous mutation within a slot operation.

Native API index<16. Bridge accepts canonical DS/CS and even SI<32; dynamic/corrupt segment/index cases execute the checked literal per-slot body as explicit compatibility, without partial native output.
Sentinel prefix has at most15 active actors for gameplay/demo scans, but reset visits all16 slots in descending order. No sign/initialized-state/timer/positive-coordinate assumptions.

All sprite/coordinate words are supported at the request boundary; executing arbitrary requests as pixels additionally requires valid original sprite/page resources. Malformed pixel resources are not made safe or normalized here.

callers: RunGameFromPassword: erase before input/update, main draw after actor/enemy/item updates, then overlays after other sprite layers.
RunScriptedDemo: erase -> interpret -> draw -> page swap. ResetSpriteEraseState is called by demo and level initialization.

bridge: Three original inline actor scan adapters; session owns all unrelated caller orchestration.

indirect.classification: Named synchronous pixel requests only. Renderer introduces no stored actor callback. All unrelated indirect dispatch remains unchanged retained L1.

owned: ActorRenderStorage: current/previous pixel X/Y, erase sprite and erase-overlay sprite. Current simulation sprite only for reset.
borrowed: Simulation fixed position and sprite/overlay outputs; no scratch aliases. Existing placement and scene initialization explicitly seed caches.
frame: Every other actor byte and physical slot, position, gameplay overlay, animation/phase state, resources and renderer globals are unchanged by the native step.
Two rolling cache generations follow alternating pages; no invented page-indexed history or mode-entry clear.
memory.projection: Bridge imports persistent words directly. Each store and pre-service cut checks the published prefix in ACTOR_VERIFY; normal completion checks final typed history and complete request consumption.

assumptions: B compares actual maintained C at complete per-slot cuts. Output covers every register/flag, current-slot RAM word, ordered store and pixel-call parameters/return word, and normal/abnormal prefixes.

Word-normalized disjoint RAM plus fixed selected-slot normalization and arbitrary-other-slot byte frame. Compiled cases cover all16 physical slots. Actor-only scans, guards and slot order remain checked retained text. Session owns nonactor orchestration; its complete caller composition is C/D.

Pixel-service bodies remain outside this unit, with their stated actor-array frame and synchronous register effects. Formal output profiles use arbitrary shared service results, including abnormal returns. Actual blits/devices are exercised by C/D and scratch host.
eliminated: Native renderer has no machine registers, addresses, memory accessors, code dispatch or sprite-directory/VGA/page layout. Native events determine what is rendered and in what order.
No dead-register/flag claim is used: the complete caller ABI and request stream are compared in the coupled session replay.
retained: Gameplay draw skips FFFF before caches, rotates both generations before signed -11<Y<192 clipping, and never clips X. Demo skips7FFF, rotates before signed X<320/Y<192 upper bounds, with no lower bounds. FFFF is not substituted for the demo hidden value.

Erase always caches the current sprite. Demo restores neither oldFFFF nor old7FFF and has no actor Y clip. Gameplay only tests oldFFFF and signed previousY<192. Overlay swap happens only after that main restore; hidden/clipped cases leave stale overlay history.
Gameplay overlay draw checks current main and overlay sprites but performs no clipping; wrapping offsets X+11/Y-13 use current caches.

Reset touches current/erase sprites for all16, retaining all four pixel caches and erase-overlay history. Explicit demo seeds touch both generations; passenger placement seeds current only; stone placement leaves caches stale.
Raw SAR5 rounds negative coordinates downward. All offsets and seeds wrap as words. Pre-update simulation reads old cached pixels, including demo-to-gameplay history.
